newsitem.title: USA: Massport to open talks for new stadium - paper.
newsitem.headline: Massport to open talks for new stadium - paper.

text.p: Massachusetts Port Authority's board voted unanimously to approve a "term sheet" setting out conditions to begin talks with the New England Patriots on a new stadium, Boston Globe reported Friday.

Massport's plan calls for leasing Robert Kraft, the football team's owner, its land in South Boston for $500,000 a year. In addition, the term sheet offers Kraft the option of developing an acre-and-a-half site across Summer Street from the proposed stadium site.

The paper said that even if the stadium is not built in South Boston, Kraft still could make a profit, as the term sheet says that if he spends $1.5 million developing the Summer Street site, he can collect up to $3 million in rent credits on the property.
That parcel is near the proposed Boston Convention center, so Kraft could build a hotel or his proposed NFL pavilion on the property.

However, the proposal to build a 69,000-seat, stadium, restaurant and NFL museum/entertainment center is a controversial one and though it is supported by Gov William Weld it is opposed by many South Boston residents.
The Patriots will face the Green Bay Packers in Sunday's Super Bowl.
